To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA binding properties and luminescence of self-assembled metallomacrocyles can be tuned by using ancillary ligands.

the DNA binding properties and the duplex DNA binding mode (i.e., inter- or intrastrand) of water-soluable, kinetically inert tetra-nuclear metallomacromolecules are controlled by judiciously selecting the ancillary ligands.

(i) the DNA binding properties and optical properties of self-assembling luminescent metallacrowns can be tuned by judicious selection and modification of ancillary ligand; (ii) the DNA binding mode and the DNA binding affinity can be tuned by the ancillary ligand, and (iii) the DNA binding affinity of the self-assembling metallacrowns is comparable to that of small molecules
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new metal-based luminescent probes for DNA, and the use of these probes as a platform for the development of new DNA-based sensors and molecular devices.
the design, synthesis, and application of self-assembled metallomacrocyclic complexes for DNA recognition and sensing.
the development of new metallacrowns and metallomacrocyclic complexes that are able to bind and detect DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ancillary ligands have a significant impact on the DNA binding properties, and that this impact is a result of the ancillary ligand's ability to modulate the overall electronic structure of the metallomacrocyclic complex.
the DNA-binding affinity and the DNA-binding mode are controlled by the ancillary ligand, the ancillary ligands, and the metal center.
the DNA binding properties and the optical responses of the tetranuclear metallodendrimers are highly dependent on the ancillary ligands used to construct them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a series of kinetically inert tetrametallic metallomacrocyclic complexes with a variety of ancillary ligand combinations.
the ancillary ligand plays a key role in determining the optical properties of the metallomacrocycle.
the binding properties of metallomacrocyclic complexes are highly dependent upon the nature of the ancillary ligands used in their assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to tune the DNA-binding properties and optical response of metallomacrocyclic complexes by changing ancillary ligands, and the binding parameters and binding modes of these complexes can be tuned by varying the metal ion.
by changing the ancillary ligand from pyridyl to imidazolyl, the binding mode of these metallomacrocyclic DNA binding ligands can be altered from intercalative to groove binding.
the DNA binding properties and optical response can be fine-tuned by judicious choice of ancillary ligand.
